note: The presence beat/eviction contract, shared by the hub (Rust) and the OS shell (TypeScript). Ticket 26/09/18 slice PR1. Measured before it existed in 🗑️generated/pr1-before-hub-socket.txt: run A shows a late joiner holding an open socket with ZERO presence frames while the other peer's roster already listed one, and run B shows BOTH rosters empty 15 s after the clients went silent, with neither socket closed.

laws.name: snapshot-deadline-fits-inside-one-beat
laws.statement: A beat never waits for the document component past its own interval: ephemeralSnapshotDeadlineMs < heartbeatIntervalMs.

laws.name: lease-outlives-three-beats
laws.statement: The hub's lease tolerates at least three consecutive missed beats before it strips a row: leaseTtlMs >= 3 * heartbeatIntervalMs.

laws.name: a-live-socket-is-always-a-row
laws.statement: Only closing the socket removes a peer from the roster. A lapsed lease drops the app-owned ephemerals (presencePack, dragGhostJson, interaction, views, ui, toolRun) and keeps the admitted identity (actor, userId, label, role, color, surface, principalKind).

laws.name: a-joiner-starts-from-the-settled-roster
laws.statement: A roster delta is published only when some peer's bytes change, so an attaching socket is handed the current roster once, before any delta, as the ONE non-delta roster frame the wire carries.

laws.name: a-moving-pointer-beats-live
laws.statement: A local window view change (pointer, camera, caret) beats the document's presence within liveViewBeatIntervalMs instead of waiting for the next heartbeat; beats caused by view changes are at least liveViewBeatIntervalMs apart, so one human adds at most 1000 / liveViewBeatIntervalMs roster deltas per second per document.
